matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns ambiguous compounding of token budgets (e.g., '8+42BT') in Section 2.1 making compute allocation unclear. None of the findings address this specific notation ambiguity or token budget compounding issue.

GT 2 concerns Table 1 showing 1B-320BT outperforming 4B-80BT under supposedly equal compute budgets with unclear normalization. Finding 7 mentions Table 1 and cherry-picking but frames it as self-critique/meta-commentary rather than identifying the underlying compute normalization issue.

GT 3 concerns contradictory claims about RL/SFT data overlap (Section 2.1 states disjoint, but Section 3.4 suggests overlap). Finding 1 identifies an epoch inconsistency in Section 3.4 but does not address data overlap between RL and SFT datasets.

GT 4 concerns the Abstract overselling CPT benefits while omitting plateaus and forgetting issues. None of the findings identify this specific claim-evidence mismatch regarding CPT effectiveness in the Abstract.

GT 5 concerns fabricated/misattributed references for FineMath and NuminaMath. Finding 2 directly identifies that FineMath is cited to two different references ([2] and [38]) with one being incorrect, matching the reference fabrication/misattribution issue.
GT 6 concerns omission of ethical considerations, IRB approvals, and bias discussion in the Abstract and methods. None of the findings address missing ethical disclosures or transparency about risks.

GT 7 concerns overgeneralized language in the Conclusion about scaling trends and ORM reliability without acknowledging limitations. None of the findings identify rhetorical overstatement in the Conclusion section.

GT 8 concerns the Abstract claiming full open-sourcing while later sections lack detailed descriptions and links. None of the findings identify this cross-section inconsistency about resource availability claims.

GT 9 concerns Section 3.4 reporting drastic RL performance drops at 350K/400K examples without disclosing training details. Finding 1 identifies an epoch inconsistency in Section 3.4's RL dataset-size experiments, which relates to the same experimental reporting issue in that section.
GT 10 concerns omission of bias assessment and fairness steps in the Method section. None of the findings address missing bias or fairness considerations in methods.
GT 11 concerns Figure 1 in Section 3.1 lacking error bars or variance reporting. None of the findings identify missing statistical uncertainty measures in Figure 1.
GT 12 concerns Section 2.2 not providing the exact computational formula or normalization for ORM score. None of the findings address missing ORM metric definition details.

GT 13 concerns Takeaways 1 and 7 ignoring reported OOD accuracy decreases at high budgets, presenting overly optimistic views. Finding 4 identifies a monotonicity inconsistency in Section 3.1 accuracy progression but does not address the takeaway claim distortion issue.

GT 14 concerns Table 4 lacking hyperparameter and evaluation method details for baseline comparisons. Finding 5 discusses Table 4 but focuses on a text-table mismatch about 'slightly better' claims, not missing comparison details.

GT 15 concerns Section 2.1 stating only final checkpoints were studied, excluding intermediate checkpoint analysis. Finding 9 mentions Section 4.1 discussing intermediate checkpoints but does not identify the protocol limitation in Section 2.1.

GT 16 concerns Section 4.1 concluding intermediate checkpoints are poor surrogates while Section 3 relies on them, creating internal contradiction. Finding 9 directly identifies this cross-section inconsistency between Section 4.1's claims and Section 3's methodology.
GT 17 concerns promotional rhetoric in the Related Work section inflating novelty. None of the findings address rhetorical tone or promotional language in Related Work.
GT 18 concerns Appendix omitting responsible disclosure and risk assessment discussion. None of the findings identify missing responsible AI or misuse considerations in the Appendix.
